dedupe_keys.name: 3d globfp global three dimensional building footprints with estimated heights 2020

description: 3D-GloBFP is a global dataset of building footprints carrying an estimated height for each building for the year 2020, described in Earth System Science Data 16, 5357 (published 2024-11-25) by Yangzi Che, Xuecao Li, Xiaoping Liu and co-authors. Heights are predicted with an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model from multisource Earth observation data and attached to existing footprint layers; the later Zenodo version adds footprints for parts of South America, Asia, Africa and Europe from Microsoft, OpenStreetMap, the VIDA Google-Microsoft combined layer and EUBUCCO. Validation across 33 subregions gives R² between 0.66 and 0.96 and root-mean-square errors between 1.9 m and 14.6 m. The paper estimates China's building volume at 5.28×10^11 m³, 23.9% of the global total. Coverage: worldwide, with one height per footprint for 2020. Access: the data are split into spatial grid tiles, each an ESRI Shapefile with heights in metres; Zenodo holds a world grid index, a readme and a list of download links. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: heights are modelled, not measured, and errors grow in regions with sparse reference data; footprints inherit the errors of their source layers. Simulation uses are building volume and floor-area exposure for flood, heat, wind and seismic loss models, and urban energy and population disaggregation. Related records: GlobalBuildingAtlas, Google Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal, EUBUCCO and Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints.
